historical_references.reference: The Qadimans were a sect of Shia Muslims in Persia, who traced their imams back to the second caliph, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. This sect emerged in the 10th century and was influenced by the Isma'ili doctrine. They believed that the imam was the manifestation of God on earth and that he would reveal himself at the end of time.
historical_references.context: Persia, influenced by Isma'ili doctrine, believed imam was manifestation of God on earth

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the Qadimans can be found in the works of the Persian poet and scholar, Ibn al-Arabi. He mentions the Qadimans in his book 'Futuh al-Makkiyya' and describes them as a group of Shia who believed in the imamate of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and his descendants, but held unique beliefs regarding the role of the imam in the world.
historical_references.context: Persia, believed in imamate of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and unique beliefs regarding imam's role
